record.original_question: How should temporal and spatial nonlocality be classified into mathematically distinct types such as memory, distributed lag, and distributed scaling, and which classes of operator kernels and corresponding fractional operators are able to model each type of phenomenon?

evidence.quote: Moreover, there is a need to classify the types of nonlocality and to link these types with the description of the types of phenomena.
It is important to solve general questions, it is important to answer the questions of what types of operator kernels (and therefore fractional operators) what types of phenomena can describe [102].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider integro-differential operators of the form
\[ (K f)(t) = \int_{a}^{t} M(t,\tau)\, f(\tau)\, d\tau \quad\text{(temporal case)}, \qquad (K f)(x) = \int_{\Omega} N(x,y)\, f(y)\, dy \quad\text{(spatial case)}, \]
including, as a distinguished family, the fractional integral and derivative operators (Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, Hadamard, Erdélyi–Kober, general Sonine-kernel operators, etc.) whose kernels depend on the difference, ratio, or more general two-variable combination of their arguments.

Three qualitatively distinct types of nonlocal behavior are to be distinguished:

(i) Memory: the value of an output at the present moment depends on a weighted history of the input on a preceding interval, with the kernel acting as a fading-memory weight.

(ii) Distributed lag: the response at the present moment is produced by inputs concentrated near one or several past instants, represented by kernels that are localized (peaked, possibly multi-modal) rather than monotonically decaying.

(iii) Distributed scaling: the contribution of past (or distant) inputs is governed by a self-similar, scale-invariant weighting, i.e. kernels that are homogeneous functions of a ratio of their arguments.

Problem. Give a rigorous mathematical classification of temporal and spatial nonlocality into the three types above (memory, distributed lag, distributed scaling), formulated as precise structural conditions on the kernel $M(t,\tau)$ or $N(x,y)$ (e.g. monotonicity, support/concentration, scaling/homogeneity properties, integrability, and admissible singularities). For each class, characterize the corresponding family of admissible kernels and identify which classes of fractional/integro-differential operators (Riemann–Liouville, Caputo, Hadamard, Erdélyi–Kober, Prabhakar, general Sonine-pair, distributed-order, variable-order, tempered, etc.) realize that class, and conversely which type of nonlocal phenomenon each such operator family is capable of modeling.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a programmatic classification problem in the theory of fractional calculus and nonlocal operators. No comprehensive classification linking kernel structural properties to memory / distributed-lag / distributed-scaling phenomena appears in the literature; surveys on general fractional calculus (Sonine kernels, Luchko, Kochubei, Tarasov) discuss partial aspects but do not provide a complete taxonomy. Status appears open.

status_evidence.title: General Fractional Calculus: Multi-Kernel Approach (Luchko)
status_evidence.snippet: Develops general fractional calculus based on Sonine kernels but does not give a phenomenological classification into memory/lag/scaling types.
status_evidence.claim: Existing general fractional calculus frameworks address kernel structure without delivering the full phenomenon classification requested.

status_evidence.title: Tarasov, Handbook of Fractional Calculus with Applications
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses memory effects and nonlocality across operator families; calls for further classification of kernel-to-phenomenon correspondence.
status_evidence.claim: The problem of classifying nonlocality types and matching them to operator kernel classes is identified as an open research direction.
